checks.label: VUL-01 · Turn on Dependabot alerts for every repository
checks.guidance: GitHub scans each repository's dependencies and raises an alert when a package has a known vulnerability. These alerts flow into ComplyJet's Vulnerabilities page.

checks.label: VUL-02 · Turn on Dependabot security updates (automatic fix pull requests)
checks.guidance: Dependabot opens pull requests that upgrade vulnerable packages, so fixes are ready to review.

checks.label: VUL-03 · Connect vulnerability findings to ComplyJet
checks.guidance: ComplyJet pulls vulnerabilities from GitHub (and cloud scanners) so they are tracked against your compliance controls.

checks.label: VUL-04 · Turn on cloud workload vulnerability scanning (AWS Inspector)
checks.guidance: AWS Inspector scans container images, Lambda functions and servers for known vulnerabilities. Needed if you run containers, serverless functions or servers.

checks.label: VUL-05 · Set fix timeframes by severity
checks.guidance: A written rule for how quickly vulnerabilities must be fixed, based on severity. Common defaults: Critical 7 days, High 30 days, Medium 90 days, Low 180 days.

checks.label: VUL-06 · Fix open vulnerabilities through reviewed pull requests
checks.guidance: Each vulnerability is fixed with a code change that is reviewed and approved by a second person before it is merged, then the alert closes.

checks.label: VUL-07 · Review open vulnerabilities regularly
checks.guidance: Someone regularly reviews open vulnerabilities across GitHub, AWS Inspector and ComplyJet, so nothing is forgotten or left past its timeframe.

checks.label: VUL-08 · Archive unused or test repositories
checks.guidance: Old, unused or test repositories are archived so they don't create vulnerability noise or hidden risk.

checks.label: DEV-03 · Anti-virus turned on and up to date
checks.guidance: Anti-malware protection is active and updating (Microsoft Defender on Windows; built-in XProtect on macOS, or a company anti-virus tool).

checks.label: DEV-05 · Operating system kept up to date
checks.guidance: Devices run a supported operating system version with automatic updates on, so security patches are applied.

checks.label: DOC-17 · Penetration test report
checks.guidance: The most recent penetration test report. Optional for SOC 2 but strengthens the report; generally expected for ISO 27001 (can be delayed short term by formally accepting the risk).

checks.label: DOC-18 · Penetration test remediation
checks.guidance: Evidence that issues found in the most recent penetration test have been fixed. Only applies once a pen test has been done.

checks.label: RSK-08 · Assess risk scenario: Vulnerabilities and root causes leading to breaches and outages are not addressed and remediated.
checks.guidance: Standard risk scenario from the ComplyJet risk library. Typical controls that reduce it: Dependabot and cloud vulnerability scanning, fix timeframes by severity, incident root cause analysis, nonconformity tracker.

checks.label: VEN-01 · Build the vendor inventory
checks.guidance: Every third-party vendor the company uses is listed, including cloud hosting, code hosting, identity/email, AI model providers, email delivery, payroll/HR, CRM, analytics and the compliance tool.

checks.label: VEN-02 · Give each vendor a risk level
checks.guidance: Each vendor is rated Low, Medium or High risk based on the data it can access and how critical it is to the service.

checks.label: VEN-03 · Assign a security owner to each vendor
checks.guidance: Each vendor has a named security owner responsible for its review and relationship.

checks.label: VEN-04 · Complete a security review for every vendor
checks.guidance: Each vendor goes through ComplyJet's three-step review: gather the vendor's security documents, summarise the findings, and record a decision.

checks.label: VEN-05 · Sign data processing agreements with vendors that handle personal data
checks.guidance: Vendors that process personal data on the company's behalf have a signed DPA (often accepted through the vendor's terms), and they appear on the company's sub-processor list.

checks.label: VEN-06 · Re-review vendors on schedule
checks.guidance: Vendors are reviewed again at least yearly, and when a new SOC 2 report is released, so no vendor is In Progress or Never Reviewed for long.

checks.label: VEN-07 · Offboard vendors that are no longer used
checks.guidance: When a vendor is no longer needed, its access and integrations are removed, company data is deleted or returned, and it is removed from the vendor list and sub-processor list.

checks.label: POL-13 · Third-Party Management Policy
checks.guidance: Protects company data and assets shared with, accessed by or managed by suppliers and other external parties. Employees must accept it.

checks.label: RDOC-01 · External non-disclosure agreement template
checks.guidance: The NDA template used when bringing on third-party vendors or partners.

checks.label: RDOC-04 · Master service agreement template
checks.guidance: The master service agreement (MSA) template used with customers, setting out services, confidentiality, data protection and security commitments.

checks.label: RDOC-05 · Outsourced development contract

checks.label: RDOC-06 · Supplier/vendor agreements

checks.guidance: Every pull request has at least one reviewer who is not the author, so nobody can approve their own changes.
